newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 26.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 26. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Supreme Audit Agency (BPK) has discovered financial losses of hundreds of billions of rupiah caused by government overspending, overpriced projects, unpaid taxes, bad loans at state-owned banks and other irregularities in state finance management.
Leading members of the Indonesian Council of Ulemas have rejected a proposal that euthanasia or mercy killing be allowed for people with AIDS.
The government will issue a deregulation package on taxation early on July.

The government is set to issue draft guidelines requiring mining companies applying for work contracts in the country to set aside a 10 percent stake to the state. The government is said to have given some 250 companies applying for contracts until Friday to accept the draft guidelines or face cancellation of their applications.
The Legal Aid Institute has supported the idea of enacting a law regulating foreign lawyers operating in Indonesia.
